*Speaking as the farmer:*

I've been at this for 35 years now, and even with my agronomy training from college, the truth is 4.5 mu doesn't leave much room for fancy experiments. My son and daughter-in-law both work in town, so the farm is more about food security and a bit of cash than feeding everyone. That actually gives me an advantage — I'm not desperate, so I can invest properly per mu instead of skimping.

I run the standard wheat-maize rotation across all 4.5 mu. Same fields, two crops a year. The turnaround between wheat harvest in early June and maize planting is the tightest week of my calendar.

**Winter wheat (already in the ground from last October):** I planted Jimai 22 — a reliable semi-dwarf for our area. Targeting around 500 kg/mu, which is realistic for my soil (medium loam, decent organic matter from years of straw return). Total N about 16 kg/mu — I put down 9 kg as base with the DAP at sowing, and I'll topdress 7 kg of urea-N at jointing in early March. P and K I apply once at base since our soil tests show adequate K. Three irrigations: green-up (early March), jointing (late March-early April), and grain-filling (early May). I might add a fourth at booting if April is dry — last year we had a dry spring and I lost about 40 kg/mu by skipping that one. Won't make that mistake again.

**Summer maize (planted mid-June after wheat):** Zhengdan 958 hybrid, no-till seeded directly into wheat stubble — saves the precious days. I shoot for 540 kg/mu. About 15 kg N/mu, with a small starter at planting and the bulk side-dressed at V6-V8. Phosphorus carries over from the wheat application so I go light. Irrigation depends on rainfall — Hebei summers usually give us enough, but I'll pump once at tasseling if July is dry.

For pesticide, I do a pre-emergence herbicide on maize (atrazine + acetochlor mix) because hand-weeding 4.5 mu of maize is more work than it's worth at my age. Wheat I scout for aphids in May and only spray if I see them.
